**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse write-only state-token render fds**

When the caller opens the shim render node with `O_WRONLY`, `drm_shim_render_node_open()` preserves that access mode for the per-open state-token memfd and then immediately registers it; this new identity path tries to validate the token by `pread64` through the caller's fd, so the parse fails with `EBADF`, registration returns `ENODEV`, and the open fails even though the code accepts the flag combination and read-only render opens work. The parse needs a readable witness for write-only state-token fds, similar to the existing helper used elsewhere, before closing the carrier fd.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid exporting state-token fds as exec locators**

When a process execs with a non-`CLOEXEC` render fd, this now picks the per-open state-token fd as the locator. The child-side locator path still validates that fd with `drm_shim_render_identity_name_parse()`, which only accepts the zero-length sealed identity-anchor memfd; a state-token fd is page-sized, so initialization returns `EBADF` and `drm_shim_identity_init()` aborts instead of preserving the shim state. Keep the locator on an identity anchor or teach the child parser to accept these tokens before exporting them here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the native ICD out of the system profile**

When this default debug profile is packaged, `build-infra/packaging/mesa-gororoba-debug-optimized/PKGBUILD:234` mirrors every installed `${_prefix}/share/vulkan/icd.d` entry into `/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d`, so enabling this option makes Meson install `r3v_native_icd.*.json` into the system Vulkan loader path (`src/amd/r300/vulkan/meson.build:379-393`). The native backend is still a bounded harness—graphics and compute pipeline creation both return `VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT` (`src/amd/r300/vulkan/r3v_native_device.c:42-68`) and the roadmap says to complete Vulkan semantics before default promotion (`docs/hardware/r3v-implementation-boundaries.md:392`)—so unpinned Vulkan apps or device-enumerating tests can see/select a second RS482 ICD that cannot run normal workloads. Keep the native ICD manifest dev-only or gated until it is ready for default enumeration.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Teach artifact-check about the native ICD**

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the calibrated model destination in tuple test**

When this test is used as the advertised golden source for the FLOAT_2 R2VB tuple, it builds the expected tuple with model destination vector 1, but the landed capture pin and calibrated producer binding use destination vector 6 (`r300_r2vb_float2_tuple_test.c` calls the interface with `0, 6`, and `R300_R2VB_CAL_MODEL_DST_VEC_LOC` is 6). This makes `check_source_tuples` pin `0x21010003` instead of the live/capture `0x26010003`, so the new source-contract check can pass while drifting away from the emitted producer PSC words it is meant to protect.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep destination-vector checks before narrowing**

When a caller passes a computed destination vector wider than 8 bits, these `uint8_t` parameters truncate it before the `> R300_R2VB_PSC_DST_VEC_MASK` checks run; for example, `256` becomes `0` and can emit a valid-looking tuple instead of failing closed. This undermines the out-of-range validation that the new tuple constructor and tests rely on, so the public arguments need a wider integer type and should only narrow after the five-bit range check.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject inadmissible source formats in tuple init**

When this helper receives a stale or hand-built `r300_r2vb_source_contract` rather than one just returned by `r300_r2vb_source_contract_init`, a `R300_VERTEX_FORMAT_F32_1` contract with self-consistent fields passes these checks and emits a five-dword PSC/VAP tuple, even though `FLOAT_1` is explicitly outside the producer contract. Since this constructor already reauthenticates the contract fields before deriving hardware words, it should also fail closed on formats outside the source policy before accepting the tuple.

In the open-gate harness, both references are unmapped when `vkQueueSubmit` runs: `record_cell` owns and unmaps the vertex mapping, and the color BO is first mapped here after the submit. That means `cache_sync_count == 2` is satisfied by the recorder's publication plus this map-establishment sync, so the test would still pass if the new queue pre/post live-mapping sync loops were removed; map a referenced memory before submitting and expect the extra pre/post counts to make the coherency verdict cover the device-access window.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Program US_OUT_FMT for the compiled color shader**

When the attended/native triangle path uses this compiled constant-color FS, the emitted IB still never sets `R300_US_OUT_FMT_0`; `r300_emit.c:687-696` programs that register sequence before draws because the ROP needs the colorbuffer output format and channel swizzle. The generated block only carries shader code plus depth/W metadata, and `r300_tcl_bypass_triangle_emit` appends only `FG_DEPTH_SRC`/`US_W_FMT`, so the draw depends on reset or stale `US_OUT_FMT_0` state instead of deterministically writing the oracle's green `0xff00ff00` value. Add the fixed `C4_8 | B,G,R,A` output-format write to the cell IB before the draw.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cover bounding-box overdraw in the oracle**

For a hardware run that fills the triangle's bounding box instead of the triangle, these exterior samples all remain sentinel while the interior samples become green, so `executed`, `interior_pass`, `exterior_pass`, and `canary_pass` can all report success even though rasterization overdraws large regions inside x=8..56/y=8..56 but outside the analytic edges. Add exterior samples inside that bounding box, or scan representative outside-triangle pixels, so this new verdict can reject that known-bad shape.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use an asymmetric color for byte-order proof**

The shader and oracle use opaque green `(0, 1, 0, 1)` / `0xff00ff00`, so an attended run cannot distinguish several byte/channel mappings: red/blue swaps, or any bug that only exchanges zero lanes, produce the same observed dword while still passing `interior_pass`. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve per-command submit evidence**

When a submit contains more than one non-empty command buffer, or when the same manifest directory is reused for multiple submits, every iteration writes the submit evidence to the same `submit_relocs.bin` / `submit_manifest.json` names, so later command buffers overwrite the bytes and digests for earlier `DRM_RADEON_CS` ioctls after those ioctls may already have run. For the attended RS482 run, this precondition is not reproducible: `four-suite run` and `recorded vector` do not name a Meson test target, command, or retained bundle, and repo-wide `rg -n "four-suite|recorded vector"` only finds this new text. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Flush caches before waiting for idle**

When this emitter is prepended to a live first draw, it waits for 3D idle before initiating the destination and Z-cache flushes, with no subsequent wait before later state and draw packets. The r300g reference sequence this table claims to preserve emits `R300_RB3D_DSTCACHE_CTLSTAT`, `R300_ZB_ZCACHE_CTLSTAT`, and then `RADEON_WAIT_UNTIL` in `src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_context.c:339-349`; preserve that order so the wait completes both flushes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject extents before unsigned addition**

For a width or height near `UINT32_MAX`, the `- 1 + R300_FDS_SCISSOR_BIAS` expression wraps to a small value, so an out-of-range extent is accepted and `scissor_word` emits wrapped coordinates. Compare the extent against the maximum unbiased size before performing the addition so every value outside the documented range returns `-EINVAL`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Model one-register PACKET0 writes**

When an input stream contains a PACKET0 header with `RADEON_ONE_REG_WR`, as emitted by `OUT_CS_ONE_REG` in `r300_cs.h`, every payload targets the base register; this loop instead distributes the payloads across consecutive registers. The checker can therefore miss the base register's final value and falsely mark neighboring contract entries as written, so register advancement must depend on the one-register bit.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check barrier placement, not just final state**

A stream that appends the expected wait and cache-control writes after its draw passes this final-value check, even though `R300_FDS_ORDERING_BARRIER` is explicitly position-sensitive and those writes no longer protect the draw. Track the draw boundary and require ordering-barrier entries in the pre-draw region; otherwise this verdict producer can certify an incorrectly ordered candidate stream.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Gate mapped-range validation and cleanup on successful setup.**

If `vkAllocateMemory` or `vkMapMemory` fails, the mapped-range child still calls flush and invalidate with a null or unmapped `live_memory`. This turns a setup failure into invalid Vulkan calls and unrelated range verdicts. The unconditional `vkFreeMemory` call also receives `VK_NULL_HANDLE` after allocation failure.

Run `call_memory_range_validation` only after allocation and mapping succeed. Record the leg as `not run` with its reason when setup fails. Free memory only when `live_memory != VK_NULL_HANDLE`.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
    void *live_map = NULL;
+   bool live_memory_ready = false;
    if (result == VK_SUCCESS) {
       result = vkMapMemory(device, live_memory, 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE, 0,
                            &live_map);
       CHECK(result == VK_SUCCESS && live_map != NULL,
             "vkMapMemory over the live allocation: %d", result);
+      live_memory_ready = result == VK_SUCCESS && live_map != NULL;
    }

-   in_child("mapped-range validation over a live allocation",
-            call_memory_range_validation);
+   if (live_memory_ready)
+      in_child("mapped-range validation over a live allocation",
+               call_memory_range_validation);
+   else
+      fprintf(stderr, "NOT RUN: mapped-range validation: allocation or map failed\n");

    if (live_map != NULL)
       vkUnmapMemory(device, live_memory);
-   vkFreeMemory(device, live_memory, NULL);
+   if (live_memory != VK_NULL_HANDLE)
+      vkFreeMemory(device, live_memory, NULL);
```

_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include ignored subproject sources in the clean-tree gate**

When Meson resolves a fallback dependency or a developer modifies an already populated `subprojects/<name>` tree, all three prescribed checks still pass: `subprojects/.gitignore:1` ignores these directories, while `git status -h` documents that ignored entries require the `--ignored` option. These dependency sources enter the build but are absent from the declared SHA; the repository's existing `require_clean_worktree()` therefore explicitly scans ignored `subprojects` at `build-infra/scripts/source_root_control.py:272-283`. Require that existing gate or an archive-derived source view instead of declaring a detached worktree clean by construction.

When the library is renamed, replaced after loading, mapped as `(deleted)`, or `/proc/self/maps` is unavailable, this helper retains `unresolved` and the submission still reaches the ioctl; an in-place replacement can instead hash bytes different from those actually mapped. When two command references carry the same GEM handle, `radeon_drm_vk_reloc_list_add` merges them into one relocation, but this table still labels each reference with its array position and labels the completion BO with `reference_count`. The resulting `bo_table` can contain more rows than `reloc_count` and assign handles to indices different from `submit_relocs.bin`, corrupting the newly claimed exact-submit identity; retain the indices returned by relocation insertion or construct the table from the final relocation list and `completion_index`.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Close evidence descriptors after fsync failures**

When `fsync(fd)` fails because of an I/O, quota, or filesystem error, the short-circuiting `||` skips `close(fd)`; unlinking the temporary path then leaves both the descriptor and its storage alive until process exit. Repeated failed retention attempts can therefore consume file descriptors and retain otherwise-hidden disk space, and the same pattern appears in `r3v_native_arming_disarm`; capture the fsync result, close unconditionally, and then return the error.

When exec keeps the same shim driver but changes its device selector—for example, a Radeon parent passes an environment with a different `RADEON_GPU_ID`—the inherited token has the same driver name but a different render marker. `drm_shim_state_token_name_parse` correctly rejects that foreign marker, but this branch converts the rejection to `EBADF`; `drm_shim_identity_init` consequently aborts instead of creating the child's newly selected identity. The existing driver-name mismatch path returns `ENOENT` for exactly this unrelated-locator case, and a marker mismatch caused by selecting another device needs equivalent handling so the child can start normally while leaving the inherited fd unclaimed.

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove isolated worktrees on every exit**

With `--isolate-worktree`, any validation, correspondence-gate, header-generation, or compilation failure after `git worktree add` calls `fail()` before reaching the success-only removal block. `TemporaryDirectory` then deletes the checkout directory but does not unregister it from Git, leaving a prunable entry under the source repository's `.git/worktrees` after every failed build; wrap the post-add work in cleanup that always runs and check the removal result.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the deployed driver authority before qualifying**

When these options are omitted or contain identities for a different deployment, the builder still publishes null or arbitrary values, while `replay_provenance_state()` in `src/amd/r300/vulkan/tests/r3v_qualification_inventory.py` checks only `correspondence_gate` and `output_sha256` before returning `verified`. A replay compiled from one kernel commit can therefore qualify results produced by a different running module, so the qualification path must require and compare these identities rather than merely record them.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L23-L27](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/7ad006c191b6e9a9bbee20883a211ea946d07baa/AGENTS.md#L23-L27)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep artifact destinations outside the supplied kernel tree**

With `--isolate-worktree`, this assignment replaces the supplied checkout path before the destination guard runs, so `--output` or `--provenance` beneath the original `--kernel-root` is compared only with the temporary checkout and is accepted. A successful isolated build can consequently overwrite or add files in the shared kernel checkout—the case the existing guard is intended to refuse—so preserve the original root and validate destinations against it before switching build roots.

**The arming report and its check assert two different vocabularies.** The runner prints the state tokens `CLOSED` and `MISMATCH` in a padded table, while the check script requires the sentences `hazard gate closed` and `not the authorized RS482 identity`. Neither sentence appears in the runner's output, so `r3v-native-direct-write-arming-runner` fails on the undeclared leg and the wrong-chip leg, and `r3v_qualification_inventory.py` line 75 then reports a missing required test. - `src/amd/r300/vulkan/tests/r3v_native_direct_write_arming_runner_check.py#L44-L48`: keep the `hazard gate closed` assertion only after the runner emits that exact string; otherwise assert the emitted `CLOSED` state token on the hazard-gate line.

nodes.title: r300: SSE3 gather candidate and three-way vertex timing bench

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Defer resource access until command execution**

When host-visible vertex data changes after command recording but before submission, this call has already copied the old values into the carrier; the shared tail also sentinel-fills the color allocation immediately, so even a command buffer that is never submitted modifies application memory. Vulkan resource reads and render-pass clears must reflect execution-time ordering, so move the gather and clear work to the submission/execution path rather than performing it in `vkCmdDraw`.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L130-L130](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/41454d8788c32ad5a138c46f5c0ff60b4bfc0ef6/AGENTS.md#L130-L130)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject a second render pass after the recorded draw**

When a command buffer records one accepted draw and then begins and ends a second matching render pass without a draw, `pass_target` is null at the second begin while the global `draw_recorded` remains true, so both calls succeed and the command buffer becomes executable. The second pass's load-op clear is silently omitted—on the first target it leaves the triangle instead of clearing it, and on another target it does nothing—so reject another begin after the cell has been recorded or track draw completion per pass.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L219-L219](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/41454d8788c32ad5a138c46f5c0ff60b4bfc0ef6/AGENTS.md#L219-L219)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Limit the clear to the image's memory range**

When the image is bound to an allocation larger than `R3V_NATIVE_TARGET_MEMORY_BYTES`, this check accepts it, but `record_triangle_cell_tail` fills `color_memory->bo.size` bytes rather than the image requirement. A valid application can bind another resource later in the same allocation, and recording a draw then overwrites that unrelated resource with the sentinel; retain the image's bound range and clear only its declared memory footprint.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Advertise only CPU-mappable image memory**

When an application chooses advertised memory type 1, `r3v_native_memory_type_policy` creates the BO with `RADEON_GEM_NO_CPU_ACCESS`, while the draw tail unconditionally maps the image allocation to perform the sentinel clear. Thus a valid binding selected from these requirements is later poisoned with `VK_ERROR_MEMORY_MAP_FAILED`; restrict `memoryTypeBits` to the host-visible type or implement the clear without a CPU mapping.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Advertise graphics support on the native queue family**

The new draw entry point cannot be used by a valid application because `r3v_GetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyProperties2` still sets `queueFlags = 0` under `R3V_NATIVE_BACKEND`. A command buffer allocated from that family therefore does not support graphics commands, so validation rejects `vkCmdDraw` even though this implementation accepts it; add `VK_QUEUE_GRAPHICS_BIT` when enabling the public recording surface.

On the native backend, `r3v_get_format_properties` derives every image and vertex feature from a Gallium screen that is absent, so it reports zero features: the exact linear B8G8R8A8 color image accepted here is reported unsupported by `vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties`, and the F32 formats accepted by pipeline creation lack `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_VERTEX_BUFFER_BIT`. Capability-aware applications and validation layers therefore reject the objects required to reach this public route; add native format capabilities matching the newly accepted image and vertex subset.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound the silicon claim to the tested carrier payload**

The existing silicon run used the fixed reference vertex bytes, while the new public route accepts arbitrary F32-family records and arbitrary in-range `firstVertex`; those inputs change the carrier BO and rasterization even though the IB digest is unchanged. The drm-shim harness only checks F32_4 and F32_3 inputs that reproduce the reference carrier, so it does not extend the silicon observation to the wider accepted input set; narrow this statement to the reference payload or retain silicon evidence for the additional carrier cases before inheriting the witness.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Destroy the public-surface harness objects before exit**

The harness exits after freeing application resources but never destroys its command pool, device, or instance. Each successful draw leaves a command-buffer-owned 4 KiB carrier and GEM handle alive until command-buffer destruction, so this test leaks all allocated command buffers and carriers and never exercises the newly added carrier-release path; resolve and call the destroy entry points in dependency order as the neighboring native harnesses do.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor semaphore waits before deferred CPU execution**

**Bound the symbol-audit claim to what the audit measures, and add its authority row.**

Two claim-precision defects in this paragraph.

The text states the symbol audit "holds the binary free of every driver symbol in any binding". `src/amd/r300/vulkan/tests/r3v_native_loader_application_symbol_audit.py` matches five prefixes at Lines 17-23: `r3v_native_`, `r3v_Cmd`, `r300_tcl_bypass_`, `r300_cpu_vertex_`, `radeon_drm_vk_`. The application source states this qualifier at its Lines 7-11; the document drops it. The "Current-source authority" table preamble at Lines 99-100 states that each current-implementation claim binds to a named Mesa source location and a structural query. The loader-boundary claim adds no row.

```diff
-against the independently emitted reference cell, while its symbol
-audit holds the binary free of every driver symbol in any binding.

+any binding, the reference SPIR-V data header being the one driver
```

✅ Addressed in commit 0d9605f

_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Bind the tail oracle to the image footprint, not to `reqs.size`.**

The comment states the clear filled "exactly the image footprint" and the seeded tail past it survived. The code uses `reqs.size` as the footprint boundary. `vkGetImageMemoryRequirements` may report a size larger than `TARGET_WIDTH * TARGET_HEIGHT * 4` because of row-pitch or allocation alignment. If `reqs.size` exceeds 16384, then `color_map[reqs.size / 4 - 1]` lies in padding the load-op clear does not touch, and the assert at Line 456 reads `COLOR_SEED` instead of `SENTINEL_PIXEL`.

The falsifier is a driver change that pads `reqs.size`; the gate then fails for a reason unrelated to clear behavior. Deriving the bound from the 64x64 B8G8R8A8 footprint makes the oracle independent of the requirements query, and an added equality assert keeps the two definitions pinned.





<details>
<summary>Proposed fix: derive the clear bound from the declared footprint</summary>

```diff
+   const VkDeviceSize footprint_bytes =
+      (VkDeviceSize)TARGET_WIDTH * TARGET_HEIGHT * 4;
+   assert(reqs.size == footprint_bytes);
    {
       uint32_t *color_map = NULL;
       assert(vkMapMemory(device, color_memory, 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE, 0,
                          (void **)&color_map) == VK_SUCCESS);
       assert(color_map[0] == SENTINEL_PIXEL);
-      assert(color_map[reqs.size / 4 - 1] == SENTINEL_PIXEL);
-      assert(color_map[reqs.size / 4] == COLOR_SEED);
+      assert(color_map[footprint_bytes / 4 - 1] == SENTINEL_PIXEL);
+      assert(color_map[footprint_bytes / 4] == COLOR_SEED);
       vkUnmapMemory(device, color_memory);
    }
```
</details>

nodes.title: r3v: prove the public route across the installed loader boundary

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Generate the arming digest for each admitted extent**

For every newly admitted non-64x64 target, this call installs an IB whose scissor payload and digest differ from the reference cell, but `r3v_native_arming_runner::cell_digest` still emits only `r300_tcl_bypass_triangle_reference_emit()`. Under the documented attended procedure, declaring the runner's 64x64 digest makes the queue reject the smaller-extent IB, while declaring the smaller digest makes the required runner check report a mismatch; consequently none of these new extents can reach hardware through the repository's authorized submission flow. Parameterize the arming runner/procedure with the extent or otherwise authorize the exact emitted variant.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L31-L34](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/58bc5dd945814bf6f2eb5dfc3257a3b4061683cc/AGENTS.md#L31-L34)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Close the render pass before checking the mismatch refusal**

This negative leg never calls `vkCmdEndRenderPass`, so `vkEndCommandBuffer` must return the refusal result for an open render pass even if the new pipeline/target extent check is absent or broken. The assertion therefore cannot verify the claimed draw-time mismatch behavior; close the pass after `vkCmdDraw` so success becomes possible unless that specific check poisons the command buffer.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the identities of the two changed IB words**

This assertion proves only that two dwords changed, not the central invariant that they are the `SC_SCISSORS_BR` and `SC_CLIPRECT_BR_0` payloads. An emitter regression that restores one scissor word while changing an unrelated register would still pass for every listed extent, even though the resulting hardware state is outside the qualified family. Record or locate the two expected payload indices and assert that every other dword is identical and that both expected words contain the resolved extent values.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L221-L223](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/58bc5dd945814bf6f2eb5dfc3257a3b4061683cc/AGENTS.md#L221-L223)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject overflowing extent arguments before narrowing**

When an operator passes a value congruent to an admitted extent modulo 2^32, such as `--extent 4294967297 20`, `strtoul()` succeeds and the cast narrows it to `1`, so the arming runner reports and can authorize a 1x20 IB instead of rejecting the out-of-range declaration. Parse into an unnarrowed type, check `errno`, the end pointer, and the admitted bounds, and only then assign the `uint32_t` values so malformed authorization input stays closed.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L26-L27](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/32c4dd0b6254865e5d5b90f9ed16e861b5caa457/AGENTS.md#L26-L27)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Name the source for the register-seam invariant**

This new public comment makes implementation-affecting architecture claims—that extent affects only `SC_SCISSORS_BR` and `SC_CLIPRECT_BR_0`, that the non-R500 bias is 1440, and that `RB3D_COLORPITCH0` can remain fixed—without naming a rank 1–4 source or marking the claims as hypotheses. Because these claims justify admitting previously unwitnessed extents to hardware, attach the applicable AMD register-guide section or exact driver/kernel source and discovery location so the admission boundary remains auditable.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L164-L171](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/32c4dd0b6254865e5d5b90f9ed16e861b5caa457/AGENTS.md#L164-L171)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require an exact value for corruption fixtures**

When either fixture variable is inherited as an empty string or `0`, the positive `r3v-native-loader-application` test still corrupts its mapped image and exits with the known-bad status, because presence alone enables these writes. This makes the known-good calibration depend on unrelated caller environment; compare against the exact fixture value `1`, as the existing IB-mutation fixture does, so only the Meson known-bad legs activate corruption.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L53-L59](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/32c4dd0b6254865e5d5b90f9ed16e861b5caa457/AGENTS.md#L53-L59)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Describe the admitted image extent family**

These new range checks make every 1..64 extent succeed, but the function comment immediately above still says creation admits exactly a 64x64 image and refuses every other shape. That comment documents the public admission boundary and now gives maintainers the opposite contract from the implementation; update it to describe the variable extent with the fixed 64-pixel row pitch and per-height footprint.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L134-L136](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/32c4dd0b6254865e5d5b90f9ed16e861b5caa457/AGENTS.md#L134-L136)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply the viewport transform for admitted extents**

When a pipeline uses any newly admitted sub-64 extent, this accepts that viewport, but `r300_tcl_bypass_triangle_extent_emit()` changes only the scissor words while `r300_tcl_bypass_triangle_vertices` remains the fixed 64x64 screen-space triangle. Because the admitted vertex shader writes its input to `gl_Position`, changing the Vulkan viewport must change the resulting window coordinates; the 48x20 case instead clips the original 64x64 geometry. Transform the gathered vertices for the selected viewport or keep these pipeline extents rejected.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L130-L132](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/0b1a4fb30f18a727ef453690df00d905d3f0546a/AGENTS.md#L130-L132)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pass the extent to the post-authorization runner**

For a non-maximum target, step 1 obtains and declares the extent-specific digest, but step 3 still runs `r3v_native_arming_runner <evidence-dir>` without `--extent`, so the runner recomputes the default 64x64 digest and reports a mismatch. Fresh evidence after the prior fix is this remaining step-3 command; document the same `--extent <w> <h>` arguments there so the repository procedure can actually arm the selected variant.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L31-L31](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/0b1a4fb30f18a727ef453690df00d905d3f0546a/AGENTS.md#L31-L31)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject NaN vertex coordinates before submission**

When the bound vertex stream contains `w = 1` but NaN in x, y, or z, every ordered range comparison here evaluates false, so the record passes the claimed clip-volume gate and NaN window coordinates reach the carrier and potentially the hardware with clipping disabled. Explicitly require finite components before applying the viewport transform so external vertex data outside the bounded domain fails closed.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L219-L219](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/2d49dec5f6199e530e29908d8d14a0d244fa251e/AGENTS.md#L219-L219)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

nodes.title: r3v: admit the reported extent range through the cell's scissor seam

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the established FP24 exponent range**

When this model qualifies the eventual RS482 producer, these bounds contradict the existing hardware-backed model in `r300_us_source_read.h:6-9,64-99`, which defines bias 62, minimum normal `0x21000000`, maximum finite `0x607fff80`, and saturation of Inf. This predicate therefore admits `2^-62` and Inf even though the producer changes their bits, while rejecting valid upper lattice values, invalidating the byte-identity oracle for those inputs. Derive admission by applying the established FP24 quantizer and comparing the result with the input instead of encoding a second range.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L164-L171](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/0ccc024db6d868431cf02e3fd3f65a2b06851145/AGENTS.md#L164-L171)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject negative normals from the RS482 identity route**

When this host route is used as evidence for an RS482 producer pass, every negative FP24 normal reaches this successful return because the sign is ignored. The silicon-measured input-register model in `r300_us_source_read.h:12-21` says a negative nonzero input arrives one FP24 ULP closer to zero, and the nominal public test stream itself contains `-0.75`, so the passing host test predicts bytes that the modeled producer will not deliver. Reject negative nonzero inputs or explicitly account for the measured source-read transform before calling this route byte-identical.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L164-L171](https://github.com/Oichkatzelesfrettschen/mesa-26-gororoba/blob/0ccc024db6d868431cf02e3fd3f65a2b06851145/AGENTS.md#L164-L171)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Decode stream components as little-endian**

On a big-endian host, this `memcpy` interprets the stream's explicitly little-endian component bytes as a native-endian integer before applying the FP32 bit masks. For example, the bytes for `1.0f` become `0x0000803f` on PowerPC and are refused even though the existing CPU gather contract supports the same byte stream there; other encodings can likewise be misclassified. Decode each component with a little-endian load before calling the predicate rather than loading it into a native `uint32_t`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent the last-record bound from wrapping**

For sufficiently large indices and strides, this purported 64-bit proof itself overflows: with `first_vertex = UINT32_MAX`, `vertex_count = 3`, `stride = UINT32_MAX`, and `size_bytes = 15`, the mathematical end is `2^64 + 15` but `last_record_end` wraps to 15 and passes, after which the domain loop dereferences offsets far beyond the declared stream. The gated Vulkan path can reach this only with an out-of-limit stride, but the common helper accepts the full-width inputs in its public contract; use the division-based check already used by `r300_cpu_vertex.c::validate` so no multiplication can wrap.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep immediate producers below the proven IB ceiling**

When callers request 1025–2047 vertices, this API admits and emits an immediate producer larger than the repository's established safe range. `r300_r2vb_immediate_producer_shape_ok()` limits this same one-input shape to 1024 vertices, and `src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_r2vb.c` records that a 2047-vertex run overflowed the whole IB and faulted; checking only the packet payload ignores the surrounding contract, prologue, and tail. When the replay tool reports an accepted stream with the wrong shape, this wildcard also passes outputs such as `verdict=ACCEPT-NO-DRAW` and never verifies the claimed `relocs=1`. When this stream is eventually submitted standalone or after an unrelated draw, it inherits `VAP_PROG_STREAM_CNTL[_EXT]` and `VAP_OUTPUT_VTX_FMT` even though the embedded body requires exactly two FP32x4 inputs and a position-plus-varying output tuple. The first-draw contract does not supply these registers, while the existing R2VB source contract and Gallium BO producer explicitly treat the complete zero-tailed PSC tuple, output formats, and `VAP_VTX_SIZE` as one load-bearing invariant; stale words can add a phantom fetch or make the VAP/GA wait for dwords this body does not contain. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Decode source lanes as little-endian before admission**

On a big-endian host with `R3V_NATIVE_R2VB_DELIVERY_EXPERIMENTAL=1`, the newly admitted F32_2/F32_3 routes misclassify valid components: `r3v_native.h` defines stream components as little-endian, but this loop copies each component into a native-endian `uint32_t` before checking its FP24 encoding. For example, little-endian 1.0 bytes become `0x0000803f` on PowerPC and are refused with `-EDOM`, so valid draws that work through the CPU route fail when the gate is enabled; load the component explicitly as little-endian before admission.

On a big-endian test host, synthesized W is stored as the byte sequence `00 00 80 3f`, so reading it through `uint32_t` yields `0x0000803f` and this new assertion fails even though delivery matches the byte-defined gather contract. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor transfer-image memory offsets**

When an allocator suballocates transfer images, `r3v_GetImageMemoryRequirements2` reports that a dedicated allocation is not required and the memory requirements expose a 4096-byte alignment, so an aligned nonzero offset is valid; this unconditional check nevertheless rejects every such bind. Standard allocation managers therefore cannot bind a second transfer image within a shared allocation. Store the bind offset on the image and include it in copy addresses, or continue requiring dedicated allocations. (`rg --fixed-strings requiresDedicatedAllocation src/amd/r300/vulkan/`)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the 16-copy recording ceiling**

When a valid command buffer records more than 16 copy regions or commands, the seventeenth operation hits this fixed capacity, poisons the command buffer, and makes `vkEndCommandBuffer` fail. Vulkan exposes no corresponding copy-region limit, so applications that batch transfers can unexpectedly lose otherwise valid command buffers; grow the operation storage dynamically and report allocation failure only when allocation actually fails. (`rg --fixed-strings R3V_NATIVE_MAX_DEFERRED_COPIES src/`)

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Implement layout transitions before accepting image copies**

When a newly created transfer image starts in `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED` or `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_PREINITIALIZED`, a valid application must transition it to `GENERAL` or the applicable transfer layout before copying. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let valid clears exceed the deferred-op capacity**

A command buffer containing 17 otherwise valid `vkCmdClearColorImage` calls fails on the 17th because `r3v_native_copy_slot()` returns `NULL` at `R3V_NATIVE_MAX_DEFERRED_COPIES` and this path poisons the recording. Vulkan exposes no command-count limit for this operation, so applications with longer transfer command buffers observe `vkEndCommandBuffer` failure despite every clear being within the advertised image family; the deferred storage needs to grow or otherwise accommodate an unbounded recording sequence.

In Arch Linux, the `conflicts` and `replaces` arrays in a package's metadata serve distinct but related roles in managing package transitions and preventing system inconsistencies [1][2]. Conflicts The `conflicts` array defines packages that cannot coexist with the package being installed because they contain the same files or provide incompatible functionality [1][2]. When pacman detects a conflict during a transaction, it will refuse to proceed with the installation until the conflict is resolved, typically by removing the conflicting package [1][2]. Replaces The `replaces` array is used to inform pacman that a new package is intended to supersede an older, existing package [2]. This is particularly common during transitions, such as replacing a legacy package with a new version or an alternative implementation (e.g., `iptables` with `iptables-nft`) [2]. When a package is marked as replacing another, pacman will generally offer to remove the old package to allow the new one to be installed [2]. Interaction and Behavior - Transaction Process: During a transaction, pacman evaluates both `conflicts` and `replaces` [1]. In these cases, users must resolve the conflict manually, for example by removing the file or using the `--overwrite` flag, though the latter is generally discouraged [1][3]. For advanced operations, tools like `pactrans` allow for granular control over how conflicts and replacements are resolved (e.g., using `prompt`, `all`, or `provided` strategies), though standard users typically rely on the default behavior of the `pacman` command [4].

The Vulkan extension VK_KHR_get_physical_device_properties2, now promoted to core Vulkan 1.1, introduced the extensible structures VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures2 and VkPhysicalDeviceProperties2 [1][2][3][4]. These structures utilize the pNext pointer chain to allow applications to query or enable additional device features and properties defined by extensions [1][4][5]. Regarding your query on pNext native memory extensions and VUIDs: 1. Mechanism: To query or enable features/properties, you construct a pNext chain starting with a base structure (e.g., VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures2) and append extension-specific structures [1][6][7]. When using these in vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures2 or vkCreateDevice, the pNext chain must be correctly configured, with the sType of each structure correctly set and unique [1][8][4][9]. 2. VUIDs: The Vulkan Specification defines numerous Valid Usage IDs (VUIDs) for these structures [8][4][9]. Common VUIDs associated with the pNext chain include: - VUID-VkPhysicalDeviceProperties2-sType-unique: Requires that every sType in the pNext chain be unique [8]. - VUID-VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures2-sType-sType: Ensures the base structure sType is correct (e.g., VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_FEATURES_2) [4][10]. - Similar VUIDs exist for specific extension structures (e.g., VkNativeBufferPropertiesOHOS, VkImportMemoryHostPointerInfoEXT) regarding sType and pNext validity [9][11][12]. 3. Native Memory: There is no single "native memory" extension; rather, various platform-specific extensions (such as VK_OHOS_external_memory or VK_EXT_external_memory_host) provide functionality for importing or exporting native memory (e.g., host pointers or OS-specific buffers) [9][11][12]. These extensions define their own structures (e.g., VkNativeBufferPropertiesOHOS, VkImportMemoryHostPointerInfoEXT) that are chained into the pNext list of memory-related structures (like VkMemoryAllocateInfo) [9][12]. For debugging specific VUID failures, ensure that all structures in the pNext chain are properly initialized, have valid/unique sTypes, and are compatible with the function being called [6]. You can verify the exact VUID for a specific error in the Vulkan Specification or by using the Vulkan Validation Layers, which report these errors during runtime [13].

**Keep the accepted bound consistent with full manifest paths.**

The new check bounds only `manifest_template`. def extract(text, name):

```shell
        print(f"{name}: NOT FOUND")
        return
    start = text.rfind('\n', 0, m.start()) + 1

    depth = 0
```

Under the Vulkan specification, it is not required that every queue family supporting VK_QUEUE_GRAPHICS_BIT also supports VK_QUEUE_COMPUTE_BIT [1][2][3]. Implementations are permitted to expose queue families that are dedicated solely to graphics operations, solely to compute operations, or solely to transfer operations [3]. In practice, this means while you may encounter "graphics-only" queue families, your application can always rely on the existence of at least one queue family that provides both capabilities [4][3]. Developers are encouraged to iterate through available queue families to find one that satisfies their specific needs—ideally one that supports both bits—rather than assuming a specific queue family index (like index 0) will always provide both [5][4].

```shell
#!/bin/bash
set -eu

python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess
from textwrap import dedent

old = r'''
function is_open_directive(line) {
  return line ~ /^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*(if|ifdef|ifndef)([[:space:]]|$)/
}
/#ifdef[[:space:]]+R3V_NATIVE_BACKEND/ {
  in_native=1
  depth=1
  print
  next
}
in_native && is_open_directive($0) {
  depth++
  print
  next
}
in_native && /^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*(else|elif)([[:space:]]|$)/ && depth == 1 { exit }
in_native && /^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*endif([[:space:]]|$)/ {
  if (depth == 1) exit
  depth--
  print
  next
}
in_native { print }
'''
new = old.replace(
    r'/#ifdef[[:space:]]+R3V_NATIVE_BACKEND/',
    r'/^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*ifdef[[:space:]]+R3V_NATIVE_BACKEND([[:space:]]|$)/',
)
```

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make cache-sync accounting safe for concurrent frees**

When two distinct mapped allocations are freed concurrently, this new call makes both threads reach `radeon_drm_vk_bo_cache_sync`, which performs an unsynchronized `device->cache_sync_count++` on the shared device. The Vulkan registry marks only each `VkDeviceMemory` parameter as externally synchronized, so freeing different memory objects concurrently is valid; this path therefore introduces a C data race and makes the production execution undefined. Make the counter atomic or keep this test instrumentation out of concurrent production paths.

This assertion observes only the final `cache_sync_count`; it never observes the GEM-close event or their relative ordering. If a later change calls `radeon_drm_vk_bo_free` before `r3v_native_unmap_memory`, the count remains `free_sync_before + 2` and the test passes even though dirty lines can be published after the BO becomes reusable—the exact regression the preceding comment says this test prevents.
